req.title: Support all HTTP verbs on /status/<code>
req.statement: The system shall accept GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE on /status/<code>.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /status/<code> must accept GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE. The source shows the route is registered for GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, TRACE (not HEAD or OPTIONS explicitly, but Flask handles HEAD automatically for GET routes). Tests must cover: (1) positive EP for each supported verb returning the exact requested status code, (2) boundary values at status code edges (100, 200, 299, 300, 400, 499, 500, 599), (3) negative paths for invalid codes and unsupported verbs. Mutation resilience requires exact status code assertions, both sides of conditionals, and coverage of the comma-branch vs single-code branch in view_status_code.

tests.name: test_options_not_in_route_returns_405
preconditions: OPTIONS is not in the route methods list
expected: Response status code is NOT 200 (OPTIONS not explicitly registered, Flask may return 200 with Allow header or 405)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-017 -> NEG: OPTIONS not in route methods -> Flask returns Allow header response, not the status_code handler
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_options_status_route_behavior():
    r = client.options('/status/200')
    # Flask auto-handles OPTIONS returning 200 with Allow header listing actual methods
    # The key assertion: it does NOT invoke view_status_code for OPTIONS
    # so the body should NOT be the status_code handler output for 200
    # Flask returns 200 with Allow header for auto-OPTIONS
    assert r.status_code in (200, 405)
    if r.status_code == 200:
        allow = r.headers.get('Allow', '')
        assert 'GET' in allow

test_options_status_route_behavior()
